title: Optimal Observable Variance Bounds beyond Quadratic Forms in Binary Experiments
banked_reason: Re-tiered from accepted on 2026-09-09: fully proved in Lean and originally accepted at field tier, but re-scored 5.7 under the recalibrated D0.5.G scale, below the 7.2 field bar; the mathematics was not refuted.

strict separation shown on one engineered witness and independent products, not a broad natural design family or school network

proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the observable Boolean-function characterization, finite pointwise conservativeness, observable-margin LP duality and Pareto complete class, and exact rational witness certificates for the 107/72 versus 55/36 quartic gap. It also formalized complement symmetry, independent-block tensorization, the HMS quadratic comparator, and conditional studentized inference with no project axioms or proof holes. Scalable school-network computation, connected-interference inference, and finite-sample coverage remain deliberately open.
tldr: A six-coordinate three-atom experiment has all-observable variance-bound optimum \(107/72\), full Boolean quadratic/cubic optimum \(55/36\), and direct Harshaw--Middleton--Savje positive-semidefinite quadratic optimum \(7/6+\sqrt{17}/9\). Thus the exact quartic gaps are respectively \(1/24\) against every observable Boolean quadratic or cubic rule and \((8\sqrt{17}-23)/72\) against the published quadratic class. The quartic optimizer has an assignmentwise nonnegative rational implementation. More generally, for fixed binary potential outcomes under a finite known randomization, expected observed-data rules are exactly the Boolean Mobius span generated by jointly observable subsets, universal conservativeness is finite pointwise domination, and the observable-margin dual characterizes the Pareto-admissible class. Complement symmetry explains the quartic threshold, and independent replication preserves the block gap. For independent triangular arrays, block independence, bounded scores, and nondegenerate average variance verify the declared Lindeberg--Feller lemma's hypotheses and yield the numerator central limit theorem; the primitive condition \(B^{-2}\sum_j\operatorname{Var}(G_{Bj})\to0\) separately yields the denominator law and asymptotically conservative studentized coverage.
gap: The closest arbitrary-design theory, \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026}, explicitly restricts the candidate bounds to quadratic forms. The zero-pairwise-inclusion correction of \cite{AronowSamii2013} supplies a conservative Horvitz--Thompson rule but not the full observable-function cone or its Pareto frontier; the binary sharp-bound papers \cite{Lu2019FactorialBinary} and \cite{AronowGreenLee2014} treat special designs and different observable information.
fill: The project leads with the exact \(107/72\) versus \(55/36\) quartic separation, then gives the if-and-only-if Boolean support theorem, pointwise conservative cone, observable-margin dual, Pareto complete class for real support probabilities, rational certificate corollary, product law, nonnegative implementation, and a bounded independent-block studentization theorem.
